topic: Synthetic data, agent traces and recirculation: evidence for a Geneva-facing game variable
horizonBasis: Assignment planning target for Geneva; the event date is not independently verified in this work.
status: Evidence review plus a proposed explanatory variable. No fitted coefficients, no forecast, no causal safety claim.

prohibited: Any single percentage for 'the Internet' that is AI-generated
A probability or year of model collapse
A statement that autonomous agents are flooding the web
A claim that benchmark rankings are corrupted by contamination
globalClaimPolicy.allowedForm: Population-scoped, detector-named, date-stamped figures, e.g. '27.5% of tokens in a June-2026 FineWeb-filtered crawl were labelled AI-generated by Pangram (S1)'.

sources.title: How Much Is an AI Token Worth? Scaling Laws for Wild AI-Generated Web Text
sources.authors: Russell, Glickenhaus, Thai, Wieting, Iyyer, Spero, Emi
sources.status: preprint; corpus WildAI (83B tokens, AI/topic/format labels) released
keyFacts: 27.5% of tokens labelled AI-generated in June 2026, 31.1% in August 2026, after FineWeb quality filtering, using the Pangram detector
800 language models pretrained at varying AI-token ratios
for data-starved models AI tokens first lower human-text loss, benefit saturates, then reverses into harm
for high human-token budgets AI tokens raise human-text loss almost immediately
replacement scaling law fits up to 3.6x larger models with 41% lower error than the best existing law
limits: one commercial detector, no reported false-positive rate on human-authored controls
English-centric filtered crawl is not 'the web'

sources.title: Delving into LLM-assisted writing in biomedical publications through excess vocabulary
keyFacts: at least 13.5% of 2024 abstracts processed with LLMs (lower bound)
up to 40% in some subcorpora
effect larger than the Covid pandemic vocabulary shift
limits: lower bound from vocabulary excess, not per-document classification

sources.title: Monitoring AI-Modified Content at Scale
sources.dataPeriod: ICLR 2024, NeurIPS 2023, CoRL 2023, EMNLP 2023 peer reviews
keyFacts: 6.5%-16.9% of submitted review text substantially LLM-modified
higher in low-confidence, near-deadline, non-responsive reviewers
limits: corpus-level maximum-likelihood estimate, not per-author attribution

sources.title: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data
sources.authors: Shumailov, Shumaylov, Zhao, Papernot, Anderson, Gal
keyFacts: early collapse loses distribution tails; late collapse converges to low variance
Gaussian case: expected Wasserstein-2 distance diverges, variance tends to 0 almost surely
no original data retained: degradation across generations
10% of original data preserved: only minor degradation

sources.title: Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data
keyFacts: replacement tends toward collapse
accumulation alongside original real data avoids collapse
finite upper bound on test error independent of iteration count
holds across sizes, architectures, hyperparameters; replicated on diffusion and VAE
limits: bounded error is not zero error

sources.title: Feature Selective Model Collapse in Diffusion Models: Total Replacement versus Fixed-Budget Training
keyFacts: fixed-budget regime (keep all data, train on fixed-size sample) degrades only partially
replacement degrades rapidly
some features lost within generations under both protocols; others preserved over unbounded horizons under fixed budget
limits: not a text or frontier-scale result

sources.title: LeakScale: Estimating the Causal Effect of Benchmark Exposure
keyFacts: 2,048 task families, 2 model families, 2 domains, 3 formulations, 589,824 generations
exposure raises exact-task accuracy by +3.22 to +10.66 percentage points
all family-clustered 95% intervals exclude zero; survives Holm correction
effect persists in all 8 paraphrase and isomorphic-transfer measurements
limits: does not establish effects on open-ended capability

sources.title: Contamination Inflates Scores but Rarely Reorders Large Language Model Leaderboards
keyFacts: 47 public models plus 74 models fine-tuned with known contamination dose
recovers dose response (+0.187 accuracy points), does not flag negative control (-0.012)
rank correlation with paraphrase-controlled leaderboard 0.997
only 3 of 188 model-by-benchmark cases show corroborated differential contamination
limits: measures differential contamination, not absolute leakage volume

sources.title: Consent in Crisis: The Rapid Decline of the AI Data Commons
keyFacts: ~5%+ of all C4 tokens fully restricted within one year
28%+ of the most actively maintained critical sources restricted
45% of C4 restricted by Terms of Service

sources.title: A Careful Examination of Large Language Model Performance on Grade School Arithmetic (GSM1k)
keyFacts: accuracy drops up to 8% on the matched benchmark
Spearman r2 = 0.36 between GSM8k generation probability and the gap
many frontier models show minimal overfitting

sources.title: WildTrace: Evaluating Training Data Detection in Realistic Large-Scale LLM Post-Training
keyFacts: best training-data detection method reaches average AUC 0.529 vs 0.5 chance in realistic SFT/DPO/RL settings
evaluation protocol choices materially change measured detection performance
limits: detection of membership, not of generation provenance

sources.title: The crawl before the fall... of referrals: understanding AI's impact on content providers
sources.dataPeriod: 19-26 June 2025, plus ongoing Radar time series
sources.status: vendor measurement with disclosed method; public API
keyFacts: crawl-to-refer ratio from Anthropic 70,900:1 to Mistral 0.1:1
native-app referrals lack a Referer header so ratios may be overstated by an unclear amount
weekly ratio changes track crawling-policy changes, e.g. Google -19.4% week-on-week

sources.title: Phi-3 Technical Report
keyFacts: 3.8B parameters, 3.3T tokens, heavily filtered web data plus synthetic data
69% MMLU, 8.38 MT-Bench

sources.title: Statistical Analysis of Synthetic Data with Verification: A Linear Regression Framework
keyFacts: tighter verification does not always lower prediction risk
a suitable level of injected generation noise can reduce risk; excessive noise increases it
full and partial fine-tuning respond differently to the same verification rule
limits: linear regression theory, not language models

sources.title: No Model Required: Text Entropy Rate Filtering Mitigates Iterative Fine-Tuning Collapse
keyFacts: six-generation QLoRA collapse experiment on Llama-3.1-8B
entropy-rate filter yields +42% unique trigrams, +30% vocabulary, -19% repetition (p<0.001)
log-probability baseline gives no significant diversity benefit (p>0.23)
filter needs no model access
limits: diversity metrics are proxies for capability

seriesInventory.question: Is there a scalable time series, or only sampled snapshots?
seriesInventory.answer: One public weekly series (crawler ratios), one 15-year annual series (excess vocabulary), otherwise snapshots or lab runs. Nothing here is extrapolable to the web as a whole.

series.reason: two points; detector error rate unpublished
regime breaks from blocking policy; endogenous

proposedVariable.name: traceLoad
proposedVariable.definition: Share of tokens newly ingested into the next training round that are model-derived.
proposedVariable.representation: interval [T_lo, T_hi]; never a point estimate

scenarioSeeds.label: scenario, not forecast
scenarioSeeds.anchor: S1 two observations; spread stands in for detector and population uncertainty

levers.name: provenance coverage
levers.definition: share of ingested tokens carrying a verifiable origin label
levers.evidence: S11 shows post-hoc detection is near chance, so labelling must happen at creation

levers.name: evaluation isolation
levers.definition: share of benchmark items never published, plus item rotation
levers.evidence: S7: exposure effects measured on unseen items; S8: 0.997 rank correlation means isolation protects level claims, not rankings

levers.name: curation retention
levers.definition: fraction of verified human-origin data retained plus diversity filtering strength

updateRule.state: T_{g+1} = clamp(T_g + alpha * (1 - p_g) * inflow_g - beta * c_g * T_g, 0, 1)

parameters.inflow_g: exogenous rate at which model-derived text enters the pool

permittedOutputs: ordering: accumulation retains more than replacement (S5, S6)
ordering: retaining verified human data retains more than discarding it (S4)
ordering: tighter curation is not monotonically better (S14)
ordering: marginal value of an AI token can change sign (S1)
prohibitedOutputs: a single prevalence number for 'the Internet'
a ranking of real countries or firms computed from these levers
causalLimits: no field or natural experiment at web scale
prevalence rests on one commercial detector with unpublished error rate
collapse evidence spans OPT-125m to 8B over few generations
crawl and consent series are endogenous to the behaviour being measured
no source separates autonomous-agent text from human-directed assistant text

gaps: no audited census of autonomous agent write-actions on the public web
no detector false-positive/negative calibration on human-authored controls at web scale
no frontier-scale test of the replacement/accumulation/fixed-budget protocols
EU AI Act Article 53 training-content summary and California AB 2013 not retrieved or verified on 2026-11-01; do not cite from memory
no measurement of AI-generated image, video or audio prevalence at web scale
Nature author correction of 2025-03-21 to S4 not read
